title: VAOM capability binding
description: Maps one agent host's tool calls onto the abstract capabilities of a Delegation Authority Matrix, and says where each fact a row needs is read from. The matrix says what is allowed; the binding says how to recognise it on a given host. It never grants anything itself: a call that no entry matches, whose capability no matrix row governs, or whose required facts cannot be read cannot be placed in a band, and an evaluator treats that as a decision failure (never allow). Passing this schema is necessary but not sufficient: the binding linter checks it against the matrix it names. Draft 0.1, a sketch.

version.description: Semantic version. Decision records cite (id, version) alongside the matrix version, so a decision can be replayed exactly.

toolSet.description: The host tool set this binding was written against, e.g. a dated host release. Reviewed whenever the host adds or changes tools; a new host tool is unmatched until then.

matrix.description: The matrix this binding is for. The linter checks it against the loaded matrix, not just the range.

versions.description: Semver range, e.g. '>=1.0.0 <2.0.0'. Recalibration bumps the matrix minor version, so an exact pin would force a binding release for every threshold change.

facts.description: Every fact the binding can produce, keyed by fact id, with its type. The names must match the matrix's requiresFacts, conditions, caps and ceilings.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the tool call's arguments. No wildcards: one pointer reads one value. Pointers address plain argument values: a wire adapter that carries each argument wrapped (ACS sends {value, provenance}) unwraps them first, so bindings stay independent of the wire format.

type.description: A value of the wrong type is treated as missing. 'money' is a decimal amount plus an ISO 4217 currency; amounts are never added across currencies.

record.description: How the fact appears in decision records. 'digest' stores a salted hash, e.g. for a counterparty or a person: caps can still group by it, and the record doesn't reveal it.

extractor.description: Where one fact's value comes from. Only the request itself or a constant written by the binding author: nothing is looked up, so the evaluator stays pure. A fact read from the arguments is only sound because those same arguments are what executes.

argCondition.description: A predicate over the call's arguments, used to split one host tool into several capabilities. String matching on free text (a shell command, a URL) is easy to evade, so a capability recognised that way is recognised at policy strength at best; prefer tools with structured arguments.

toolEntry.description: Recognises some calls of one host tool as one capability. A call may match several entries: it then takes every matched capability, and its band is the strictest across them. So an extra entry can only narrow what a call may do. A call that matches no entry is unmapped.

toolPrefix.description: Tool-name prefix, for tool families such as one MCP server's tools.

capability.description: A capability id from the matrix. Exactly one matrix row must govern it. The binding alone decides a call's capability: a capability the host or framework declares on the wire is never trusted for authority, and one that disagrees with the binding makes the call unplaceable.

items.description: For batch tools. Each element of the array at 'arg' is evaluated as its own action, with its own facts plus the per-call ones. The call's band is the strictest across its items, and every item counts toward cumulative caps, so batching can't slip under a per-action ceiling. An empty or missing array means the call can't be placed.

additionalProperties.description: Pointers here are relative to the item.
